per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window with an ordered core. Protonated free GB3 at 24 °C has ordinary fast backbone motion (F30 S2 0.81-0.93 depending on the CSA model; GB3-J1, r2). The Hall and Fushman 2003 data (24 °C, pH 5.8, 600 and 400 MHz), read in full, and the 2010 reanalysis place the largest fast motion in the beta1/beta2 loop K10-E15, the helix-beta3 loop D40-G41, Q2, A20 and A48 (J2; r10, 17-r1), and 30 secondary-structure residues average S2 about 0.89 (J3, r10). ILV methyls move on the sub-ns scale, more in perdeuterated than in protonated GB3 (J4, r17; J5, r18). Weaker items: GB1 homolog loops (J6, r4), SRLS model dependence at Y3, L12 and A26 (J7, r33, abstract-only) and pulse-sequence artefacts in a perdeuterated sample (J8, r8). The paper behind BMRB 5839 is not named in any source; the deposited set matches the 2003 sample (J43).
per_window.us-ms: WT apo by amide 15N at room temperature: nearly silent. In the 2003 data (24 °C, pH 5.8) the helix Rex seen under isotropic tumbling is an anisotropy artefact (J15, 17-r2), V39 is the one consistent exchange site (Rex 0.28-0.78 s-1 by model; J44, 17-r3; five fields, J13, r3), K13, G9 and T49 are unconfirmed (J45) and seven other small Rex terms are model or structure bias (J46); relaxation-compensated CPMG up to about 8 ms finds nothing (J18, 17-r4), and 15N broadening is about 0.15 s-1 or less at 900 MHz, 25 °C (J14, r26). Multiple-quantum probes in protonated WT at 25 °C report slow correlated shift fluctuations: Calpha-Cbeta kex about 100-160 s-1 at 17 residues (J9, 15-r4) and C'-N kex about 110-430 s-1 over most of the backbone (J10, 15-r2); perdeuterated controls J11 and J12. Microsecond exchange is detected only in perdeuterated, cold GB3: the first-turn amide protons G9-K13 share tau_ex 35.9 µs at 262 K down to 9.1 µs at 275 K (J47, 17-r5 to 17-r8; individual fits 7-16 µs at K10, L12, K13, J51, 17-r18), while amide 15N and protons outside the turn stay flat (J48, 17-r10, 17-r11); seven ILV methyl carbons exchange with tau_ex 11-58 µs at 275 K, the proton only at V54 (J50, 17-r16, 17-r17, 17-r19). The T11K/K19E/V42E mutant shows temperature-sensitive R1rho at N8, T16, T17, N37 and T53 (J17, r9, inference_from_mutant); a protein G domain II homolog shows the same tumbling artefact (J16, r6).
per_window.slower_than_ms: Only the E27Q mutant has H/D exchange: beta2 amides exchange within the 0.5 h dead time and their beta1 partners over hours at 298 K (J41; r46, r47; inference_from_mutant). WT HDX, cis-trans and other slow methods were not found by narrow zero-hit searches (J42, search_insufficient).
per_window.undetermined: Motions slower than tumbling without a measured room-temperature rate. The first-turn lifetimes extrapolate to 371 ± 115 ns (Arrhenius) or 409 ± 126 ns (Eyring) at 310 K, between the ps-ns and us-ms windows (J19, 17-r9, r20), and RDC-derived supra-tau_c amplitudes peak in the same turn (J49, 17-r12). CCR plus RDCs show correlated bond fluctuations slower than tumbling (J20, r35; J21, r36) and loop/helix correlation patterns (J22, r12; J23, r13, md_only); charge-mutant RDCs put the largest NH fluctuations in beta2 and at K10-L12 (J24, r7); a beta4 RDC excess is unresolved against measurement error (J25, 15-r10); L12, D40 and G41 are repeatedly cited as flexible (J26); abstract-only RDC ensembles agree qualitatively (J27). Side chains: 26 residues populate two or three chi1 rotamers and 17 fit one (J28, J29; r15, r37), F52 is contested (J30, r38), and crystal alternates partly match (J31, r16, structure_only). Also here: IPAP coupling artefacts (J32), abstract-only accelerated MD (J33), free versus Fab-bound crystals without major change (J34), osmolyte H-bond strengthening (J35), dielectric screening with K19 mutants (J36), and isolated peptide ensembles (J37-J40, md_only). Not judged: overall tumbling (r11; TRACT tau_c 3.6 ns at 298 K, 17-r15), the RDC-restrained ERMD ensemble and static/ensemble structure comparisons that restate the first-turn pattern without a rate (17-r13, 17-r14), methods-only abstracts (r22, r23, r24, r25, r34, r40, 15-r1, 15-r11), side-chain coupling abstracts (r39, 15-r9), MD-CSA abstract (r19), SRLS review (15-r14), GB1, GB2 and protein G'e structures or footprinting (15-r12, 15-r13, 15-r23, 15-r24, 15-r31), AlphaFold comparison (15-r32), SAXS hydration and restrained hydration MD (r48, r49, r50), osmolyte REMD (r57-r60) and dielectric MD (r63-r65).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Not as population-resolved exchange: in protonated wild-type GB3 alone, 15N amide relaxation at 24 °C, pH 5.8 (9.4 and 14.1 T) finds exchange only at V39 (Rex 0.28-0.78 s-1 depending on the tumbling model), shows that the elevated helix R2 comes from anisotropic tumbling, and sees no CPMG dispersion up to about 8 ms, while multiple-quantum CSM/CSM relaxation at 25 °C, pH 7.0 reports slow correlated shift fluctuations (Calpha-Cbeta at 17 author-listed residues, kex about 100-160 s-1; C'-N over most of the backbone, about 110-430 s-1) with no population or minor state; the microsecond first-turn exchange (G9-K13, tau_ex 9.1-35.9 µs) and methyl exchange at seven ILV residues were measured only in perdeuterated GB3 (methyls at 275 K; first turn at 262-275 K), and the 371-409 ns lifetime at 310 K is an extrapolation.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 5839 holds one 600 MHz R1/R2/NOE set at 297 K, pH 5.8 for 51 residues (E15, T25, E27 and N35 absent); NOE below 0.65 marks Q2, K10-K13, D40 and G41 as fast-moving, and R2/R1 above the 2.405 cut flags K28, K31, Q32, D36 and V39. Under the screen's own caveat, the helix flags fit the anisotropic tumbling that Hall and Fushman 2003 identified, leaving V39 as the flag that literature also calls exchange.
open_conflicts: Backbone ps-ns amplitude heterogeneity: the five-field Fushman analysis finds large site-to-site 15N CSA variation that moves F30 S2 from 0.93 to 0.81 (r2), while the RCSA-calibrated Bax analysis finds near-uniform S2 0.888 ± 0.017 versus 0.892 ± 0.025 with either CSA treatment (r10); the row notes the discrepancy is not settled by choosing one study.

V39 exchange: Rex at all five fields at 24 °C, pH 5.8 (r3) and in every tumbling model at two fields (0.28-0.78 s-1, 17-r3) versus backbone 15N broadening of about 0.15 s-1 or less at 25 °C, pH 6.3 (r26); r26 does not say whether V39 is an exception, and the samples differ in pH.

The protonated Calpha-Cbeta kex of 100-160 s-1 (-r4) uses the perdeuterated sample as an approximate CSA baseline (-r5), so if deuteration itself suppresses the slow motion the baseline and the rate are coupled.
F52 side chain: single rotamer in the RDC analysis (r15) versus slight averaging in some scalar couplings that the compilation excludes (r38).

Probe contrast, not a conflict: at 275 K the first turn disperses on amide 1H (J47, J51) but not on 15N (J48), and seven ILV carbons disperse while only V54 does on the methyl proton (J50); the authors attribute this to shift contrast at each nucleus.
questions_for_gina: Is the RelaxDB 5839 R1/R2/NOE set the Hall and Fushman 2003 deposition? The deposited conditions (297 K, pH 5.8, 600 MHz, E15, T25, E27 and N35 absent) match that paper, but no source names the accession.

Should the WT apo us-ms answer count the multiple-quantum kex bounds (protonated, 25 °C) and the first-turn and methyl microsecond exchange measured only in perdeuterated GB3 at 262-275 K, or only room-temperature amide 15N data, which show exchange at V39 alone?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Row-id shorthand in this file: 15-rN = GB3-5839_20261015212628-rN, 17-rN = GB3-5839_20261017120337-rN, rN alone = GB3-rN. Almost every GB3 NMR sample uses 10-50 mM sodium or potassium phosphate at pH 5.8-7.0 and 22-25 °C, at high protein concentration (1.3-5 mM); no row establishes a phosphate artefact for GB3, and no buffer comparison exists. Perdeuterated or triple-labelled samples (r8, r18, r36, 15-r3, 15-r5, and the 2015/2016 high-power R1rho rows 17-r5 to 17-r19) are flagged is_wt_apo false because deuteration measurably changes GB3 methyl amplitudes (r17 versus r18) and the slow Calpha-Cbeta signal; the high-power R1rho samples (3 mM, 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.5, 100 mM NaCl) were also measured at 262-275 K, with 262-269 K supercooled in capillaries. Aligned samples (Pf1, PEG, bicelles) and charge mutants used for RDCs (r7, r15, r35, r36, r37) are likewise not WT apo isotropic states. The entry sequence carries Q2 (M1/Q2 replace native T6/T7). RDC and CCR rows report motion slower than tumbling without an upper rate, so they stay in the undetermined window.
